pr_title: ENGINE_load_private_key(): Do foreign key detection without side effects
pr_body:
Doing set1()/get1() has unwanted side effects.
Instead just set the foreign flag appropriately.

Fixes #22945
pr_comments: This seems to fix segfaults I'm getting signing with my yubikey with `sbsign`, `pesign`, as well as using the `org.openssl.engine:` notation with `openssl dgst` with libp11 or ykcs11.

Sorry, no. It breaks the problem originally fixed: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/19965#issuecomment-1382889805 

I'm sorry that I approved it before without testing. #22977 seems working.

@beldmit I do not think the other approach is right. Instead I would like to know why this patch does not work. Can you please identify why setting the foreign key bit does not work with this patch? IMO we ideally have testcases in the codebase for this and they should have been added with the first fix.
I think I got it. the NSS engine doesn't deal with EVP_PKEY_METHOD, it uses old-style RSA_METHOD/EC_METHOD etc. So the assignment of the low-level object stores the linked RSA_METHOD in the struct.

> I think I got it. the NSS engine doesn't deal with EVP_PKEY_METHOD, it uses old-style RSA_METHOD/EC_METHOD etc. So the assignment of the low-level object stores the linked RSA_METHOD in the struct.

Then it needs to actively create the EVP_PKEYs as legacy and not just assume d2i_PUBKEY will produce legacy keys. But I see the current code of e_nss already fixed that.
@t8m how do you run tests? I tried to test your patch with e_nss 4.3 but didn't manage to initialize the database...
@beldmit I did not run tests I just looked at the e_nss source in their repo in gitlab.

I managed to run the test, it passes. 
I don't like that we enforce the authors of engines to update their code and lose the attached `*_METHOD`s but as we don't have proper tests, let's live with it.

@beldmit this is misunderstanding - we should actually revert https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/2b74e75331a27fc89cad9c8ea6a26c70019300b5 completely. This PR is not right. 

The foreign flag would be detected properly anyway when the key is created _properly_, i.e. by EVP_PKEY_set1_RSA() inside the engine or by having a non-default EVP_PKEY method.

Yet another post factum correction. 
The real , as is pointed in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/19965#issuecomment-1399592137 is to improve decoder do not touch "external(foregin)" keys.

> The real , as is pointed in [#19965 (comment)](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/19965#issuecomment-1399592137) is to improve decoder do not touch "external(foregin)" keys.

The question is what do you mean @petrovr by "external(foreign)" keys in this context. What I see that e_nss is doing simply cannot work properly because it calls d2i_PUBKEY() and it expects that key to be something "externally managed" that is simply impossible to do by default and it would break all expectations that keys are by default something managed by providers and the foreign keys are exceptions. However what I see in the current e_nss code is that the get1/set dance is being done so I do not see why we would need this incorrect workaround anymore. IMO it should be reverted. Possibly we could keep the foreign key set up as of #22951 but maybe it is unnecessary as the foreign key flag should have been already set when the engine creates the key.

What is "external(foreign)" key - attributes set on structure internal to the cryptographic library ( brief details in  https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/19965#issuecomment-1399592137 ) in case of classical key management (pre 3.0).
Also comment is my objection to proposed and now committed correction. 

So nevertheless that internal structure has attributes set as for key that cannot be managed by provider key is imported to provider store. As expected exported key lost all those attributes.

----
E_NSS engine always will use work-around for all 3+ releases.
It seems to me engine mentioned in this issue is based on PKEY functionality.

> It seems to me engine mentioned in this issue is based on PKEY functionality.

Yes, it is.

review_comments:
There is a change in behavior with the new code: `EVP_PKEY_SM2` simply breaks out of the `switch` without doing anything. The original code at least tried to see if it was an EC key.
It also means that `pkey->foreign` is never set for `EVP_PKEY_SM2`.
Fixed @beldmit please re-approve. IMO we actually do not want to change the key type here but yeah, the foreign key detection for SM2 seems broken so... Although I would be very much surprised if there were any engines which work with SM2 keys.
Still approved if fixes #22945
